reaction_mechanism_logic: The study of different organozinc reagents revealed a structure-activity relationship where Me2Zn, while less reactive than Et2Zn (requiring 67 h vs 15 h), provided superior enantiocontrol (94% ee vs 88% ee). This suggests that the smaller methyl group allows for a more selective transition state within the chiral environment of the copper-Schiff base complex.
influence_analysis: The use of Me2Zn as the nucleophile significantly increases the enantioselectivity to 94% ee, although it necessitates a much longer reaction time (67 h) due to its lower inherent reactivity compared to Et2Zn. This demonstrates a clear reactivity-selectivity trade-off based on the steric bulk of the R group on zinc.

reaction_process_description: The desymmetrisation of the six-membered ring substrate, meso-2-cyclohexene-1,4-diyl bis(diethyl phosphate) (4), was performed using phosphoramidite ligand 2c. Substrate 4 (1.0 equiv.) reacted with Et2Zn (2.0 equiv.) in toluene at -40 °C for 15 hours in the presence of [Cu(OTf)]2·C6H6 (0.05 equiv.) and ligand 2c (0.2 equiv.). The reaction yielded the inversion product ent-7a in 69% isolated yield with 94% ee, and a regioselectivity ratio (inversion/retention) of 85:15.
reaction_mechanism_logic: Schiff base ligands were found to be ineffective for six- and seven-membered ring substrates. Phosphoramidite ligands (2) were employed instead. Ligand 2c, which combines (S)-BINOL with an (S,S)-diamine moiety, was identified as the 'matched' combination for substrate 4, providing high enantioselectivity at -40 °C. The authors noted that higher temperatures generally favored the formation of the racemic retention product 9.
influence_analysis: The switch to phosphoramidite ligand 2c is essential for the successful desymmetrisation of the six-membered ring substrate 4. The specific 'matched' stereochemistry of the ligand and the controlled temperature of -40 °C are the primary factors driving the high enantiomeric excess (94%) and favoring γ-substitution with inversion.

reaction_process_description: For the seven-membered ring substrate, meso-2-cycloheptene-1,4-diyl bis(diethyl phosphate) (5), the reaction was carried out with Et2Zn (2.0 equiv.) in toluene at -40 °C for 15 hours. The catalyst was formed from [Cu(OTf)]2·C6H6 (0.05 equiv.) and phosphoramidite ligand 2b (0.2 equiv.). This procedure yielded the inversion product ent-8a in 85% isolated yield and an exceptional enantiomeric excess of >98%.
reaction_mechanism_logic: The seven-membered ring substrate 5 exhibited the highest levels of selectivity in the study. Using phosphoramidite ligands 2b or 2c, the reaction proceeded exclusively via γ-substitution with inversion, yielding virtually a single enantiomer. This demonstrates the high efficiency of the copper-phosphoramidite system for larger meso-cyclic allylic systems.
influence_analysis: The combination of the seven-membered ring geometry and the phosphoramidite ligand 2b results in near-perfect enantiocontrol (>98% ee). The increased ring size compared to 3 and 4 appears to facilitate a more rigid or well-defined transition state in the presence of the bulky phosphoramidite-copper complex.

reaction_process_description: The desymmetrisation of the conduritol derivative 10 (1.0 equiv.) was achieved using Et2Zn (2.0 equiv.) in toluene at -60 °C. The reaction utilized [Cu(OTf)]2·C6H6 (0.05 equiv.) and phosphoramidite ligand 2b (0.2 equiv.). To improve the yield, the reaction time was extended to 72 hours. The product 11a, a highly functionalized cyclohexane with four contiguous stereocenters, was obtained in 52% isolated yield (74% based on recovered starting material) with 86% ee.
reaction_mechanism_logic: Substrate 10, being more sterically hindered and functionalized, required the more reactive phosphoramidite ligands (Schiff bases were ineffective). The authors observed that while the reaction was slow, extending the time to 72 hours allowed for a practical yield of a single diastereomer. The absolute configuration was assigned by analogy to the six-membered ring products.
influence_analysis: The extended reaction time (72 h) is the critical optimization variable for substrate 10, overcoming the steric hindrance of the acetal-protected diol moiety. The phosphoramidite ligand 2b provides the necessary reactivity and stereocontrol to generate a complex chiral building block from an achiral precursor in 86% ee.

reaction_process_description: In this optimization reaction, benzaldehyde (1 mmol) was reacted with ethyl 2-bromoacetate (1.2 mmol) and 2 equivalents of 20-30 mesh zinc granular. The reaction was performed in a 10 mL grinding jar with a single 4g stainless steel ball at a frequency of 30 Hz for 2 hours under neat (solvent-free) conditions. The product, ethyl 3-hydroxy-3-phenylpropanoate, was obtained with 97% conversion and an 81% NMR yield (72% isolated yield). The structure was confirmed by 1H NMR analysis using mesitylene as an internal standard.
reaction_mechanism_logic: Condition optimization revealed that increasing the zinc amount from 1.6 to 2.0 equivalents significantly improved the yield from 70% to 81%. However, further increasing the zinc to 5 equivalents or the halo-ester to 2 equivalents did not lead to significant yield improvements. Time-course studies (0.5 h to 2 h) established that 2 hours of milling are required for complete conversion, as shorter times resulted in lower yields (e.g., 33% at 0.5 h).
influence_analysis: The amount of zinc is a critical optimization variable; 2 equivalents are necessary to ensure high conversion. The mechanical energy provided by the 30 Hz milling frequency acts as the activation method, successfully bypassing the need for chemical activators or inert atmospheres by continuously exposing fresh zinc surfaces.

reaction_process_description: This reaction evaluated the effect of the zinc source morphology. Benzaldehyde (1 mmol) and ethyl 2-bromoacetate (1.2 mmol) were reacted with 2 equivalents of zinc flake (~325 mesh) at 30 Hz for 2 hours in a mixer mill. The reaction proceeded with 99% conversion and achieved the highest NMR yield of 87% among the tested zinc forms.
reaction_mechanism_logic: The authors screened 12 different physical forms of zinc (granular, foil, dust, shot, flake, wire, powder, mossy). The trend observed is that zinc forms with a higher surface area to volume ratio (like flakes and fine powders) perform better under neat ball milling conditions. This is attributed to the more efficient mechanical breakdown of the zinc oxide layer and better mixing of the high-surface-area metal with the liquid reactants.
influence_analysis: The physical form of the zinc source significantly influences the reaction efficiency. Zinc flakes (~325 mesh) provided an 87% yield compared to only 53% for zinc shot, demonstrating that higher surface area facilitates faster and more complete formation of the organozinc intermediate under mechanical stress.

reaction_process_description: To test functional group tolerance, 4-bromobenzaldehyde (1 mmol) was reacted with ethyl 2-bromoacetate (1.2 mmol) and 2 equivalents of zinc flake (~325 mesh) under the optimized milling conditions (30 Hz, 2 h). The corresponding β-hydroxy ester was isolated in 82% yield.
reaction_mechanism_logic: The study of substrate scope for carbonyl electrophiles showed that the mechanochemical Reformatsky reaction is highly chemoselective. Specifically, aryl halides (Cl, Br) and trifluoromethyl groups are well-tolerated.
influence_analysis: The use of ball milling allows the reaction to occur under mild, solvent-free conditions, which prevents side reactions like hydrodehalogenation that are sometimes observed with more reactive organometallic methods. This highlights the 'mild' nature of the in situ generated organozinc species.

reaction_process_description: In this reaction exploring latent nucleophiles, benzaldehyde (1 mmol) was reacted with ethyl 2-bromopropionate (1.2 mmol) and 2 equivalents of zinc flake (~325 mesh) at 30 Hz for 2 hours. The product was obtained in 67% isolated yield as a mixture of diastereoisomers.
reaction_mechanism_logic: The authors investigated the scope of α-halo esters and related compounds. Substituted α-halo esters like ethyl 2-bromopropionate successfully form organozinc intermediates in situ, though the mechanochemical environment provides only moderate diastereocontrol.
influence_analysis: The introduction of a substituent at the α-position of the halo-ester (moving from ethyl 2-bromoacetate to ethyl 2-bromopropionate) slightly decreases the yield (from 72% to 67%) and introduces diastereoselectivity issues, reflecting the increased steric bulk at the reacting center.

reaction_process_description: A control reaction was performed in solution to compare with the mechanochemical method. Benzaldehyde and ethyl 2-bromoacetate were reacted in dry THF under a nitrogen atmosphere at 50 °C for 2 hours using either zinc flakes or granular zinc, without any chemical additives.
reaction_mechanism_logic: This experiment was designed to demonstrate the necessity of mechanical activation. In the absence of ball milling, the passivating oxide layer on the zinc prevents the reaction from proceeding efficiently in conventional organic solvents.
influence_analysis: The comparison shows a stark contrast: 87% yield with milling versus 7% in solution. This confirms that the mechanical energy in the ball mill is the primary driver for activating the bulk zinc metal, making the process 'greener' by eliminating the need for dry solvents, inert gases, and corrosive chemical activators.

reaction_process_description: This reaction involves the Pd-catalyzed conjugate addition of dialkylzinc reagents to conjugated enals. The process uses 5 mol% of a Pd(OAc)2/PPh3 precatalyst system in THF solution. The reaction is conducted at temperatures ranging from -78 to -20 °C, providing 1,4-adducts in good to excellent yields. The intermediate zinc enolates can be trapped by quenching with TBSOTf to yield (E)-enol silanes.
reaction_mechanism_logic: The authors found that while the reaction proceeds without the PPh3 ligand, its addition is crucial for practical purification, as it prevents the precipitation of persistent palladium by-products. The mechanism involves a Pd-catalyzed 1,4-addition that selectively avoids competing 1,2-addition to the aldehyde group. However, the method is limited to enals, as conjugated acyl oxazolidinones, nitriles, and esters were found to be unsuccessful substrates.
influence_analysis: The use of the PPh3 ligand significantly improves the workup and purification process by stabilizing palladium species. The reaction temperature (-78 to -20 °C) is critical for maintaining regioselectivity for 1,4-addition over 1,2-addition.

reaction_process_description: In this catalyst-free procedure, allylzinc and benzylzinc reagents undergo conjugate addition to β-nitroalkenes. The reaction is performed under solvent-free conditions at room temperature, yielding the desired β-substituted nitroalkanes in moderate to good yields.
reaction_mechanism_logic: The optimization logic highlights the necessity of solvent-free conditions; when the reaction with benzylzinc bromide was attempted in THF, no 1,4-addition product was formed. The electronic nature of the substrate also plays a role: electron-withdrawing groups on the phenyl ring of nitrostyrenes decrease the yield, whereas electron-rich heterocyclic nitroalkenes provide higher yields.
influence_analysis: The absence of solvent is the defining factor for the success of the benzylzinc addition. The reaction rate and efficiency are positively influenced by electron-rich substrates.

reaction_process_description: This reaction describes the addition of lithium tetraorganozincates (R4ZnLi2) to nitroolefins using a deep eutectic solvent (DES) composed of choline chloride and D-(-) fructose. The reaction is ideally performed at 0 °C under a nitrogen atmosphere to produce the conjugate addition product with up to 98% yield.
reaction_mechanism_logic: The authors observed a reactivity-selectivity trade-off: at 25 °C under air, a substitution by-product (where the nitro group is displaced) was formed in significant amounts (up to 20%). Lowering the temperature to 0 °C and strictly excluding air suppressed this side reaction, making the 1,4-addition the sole pathway. The lithium tetraorganozincates were prepared in situ by mixing 2 equivalents of RLi with R2Zn.
influence_analysis: Temperature and atmosphere are the primary variables controlling chemoselectivity. The use of a Deep Eutectic Solvent provides a sustainable medium that facilitates high reactivity for the zincate species.

reaction_process_description: This reaction involves a tandem conjugate addition-cycloallylation of dialkylzinc reagents to enones possessing appendant allylic carbonates. The reaction is promoted by 1 equivalent of ZnI2 in DCM at 35 °C, resulting in the formation of 5- and 6-membered rings with three new stereogenic centers.
reaction_mechanism_logic: The mechanism proceeds via an intermediate zinc enolate that undergoes an intramolecular SN2'-type substitution of the allylic carbonate. The authors noted a structure-activity relationship where iPr2Zn provided higher yields than Et2Zn due to the higher reactivity of the isopropyl group in the initial conjugate addition step. The choice of additive is specific; using Bu4NI instead of ZnI2 reduced the yield.
influence_analysis: The steric bulk of the R group (isopropyl vs ethyl) enhances reactivity. The presence of the iodide source (ZnI2) is essential for the tandem cyclization efficiency.

reaction_process_description: A catalyst-free conjugate addition of aryl and alkylzinc halides to nonenolizable unsaturated ketones. The reaction is conducted in 1,2-dimethoxyethane (DME) at 50 °C. The organozinc halides are prepared via direct zinc insertion into organic halides in the presence of LiCl.
reaction_mechanism_logic: Optimization of the solvent was key. DFT calculations revealed that DME, possessing two oxygen atoms, chelates the lithium cation in the transition state. This chelation lowers the activation energy significantly compared to THF, allowing the reaction to proceed efficiently without a transition metal catalyst.
influence_analysis: The coordinating ability of the solvent (DME) is the decisive factor for overcoming the kinetic barrier in the absence of a catalyst.

reaction_process_description: This is an asymmetric conjugate addition of dialkylzinc reagents to cyclic enones to form products with two quaternary stereogenic centers. The reaction uses CuCN as a catalyst and a chiral anthranilic acid-based ligand in toluene at -15 to 0 °C.
reaction_mechanism_logic: This was the first reported enantioselective conjugate addition to tetrasubstituted olefins. An interesting observation was made regarding solvent purity: undistilled toluene provided higher enantioselectivity than purified solvent, suggesting that trace components or the specific state of the solvent environment influenced the chiral induction.
influence_analysis: The ligand design is critical for creating quaternary centers. The counter-intuitive benefit of undistilled toluene highlights the sensitivity of the asymmetric catalyst system to the reaction environment.

reaction_process_description: This reaction features the asymmetric conjugate addition of a catalytically generated zinc homoenolate to an α,β-unsaturated ketone. The homoenolate is formed in situ from a cyclopropanol derivative using Et2Zn and a chiral β-amino alcohol. The reaction uses DMPU as a Lewis base and molecular sieves as additives, followed by heating to 100 °C to effect an intramolecular aldol condensation.
reaction_mechanism_logic: The mechanism involves the formation of a mixed zinc alkoxide which undergoes ring opening to a homoenolate. This species then coordinates to the enone for the asymmetric 1,4-addition. The authors utilized DMPU to modulate the Lewis acidity/basicity of the zinc species. If the conjugate addition is slow, a proton abstraction side-pathway can occur, but this is managed by the catalytic cycle that regenerates the active zinc alkoxide.
influence_analysis: The chiral β-amino alcohol is the source of asymmetry, while the temperature ramp (0 to 100 °C) is necessary to drive the subsequent aldol cyclization to the final cyclopentene product.

reaction_process_description: In a typical optimization experiment, phenylzinc bromide was generated in situ by reacting phenyl bromide (0.75 mmol) with n-butyllithium (0.80 mmol) in diethyl ether at room temperature for 0.2 hours, followed by the addition of zinc bromide (0.75 mmol) and stirring for an additional 0.5 hours. To this suspension, N,O-acetal 1a (0.50 mmol) and freshly distilled chlorotrimethylsilane (Me3SiCl, 0.60 mmol) were added. The reaction mixture was stirred at room temperature for 1 hour. Upon completion, the reaction was quenched with a saturated aqueous solution of Na2CO3, extracted with chloroform, dried over anhydrous Na2CO3, and purified by silica gel column chromatography to afford the α-phenylglycine derivative 2a in 93% isolated yield.
reaction_mechanism_logic: The reaction mechanism relies on the activation of the N,O-acetal by Me3SiCl. Organozinc reagents possess lower nucleophilicity compared to Grignard or organolithium reagents, making them generally unreactive toward N,O-acetals under standard conditions. Me3SiCl acts as a Lewis acid promoter that coordinates to or reacts with the methoxy group of the acetal, facilitating the formation of a more reactive iminium-type intermediate or enhancing the leaving group ability of the methoxy moiety, thereby allowing the nucleophilic organozinc species to attack and form the C-C bond.
influence_analysis: The presence of Me3SiCl is mandatory for the reaction; without it, the starting material 1a is recovered (Entry 3). While Hf(OTf)4 was initially tested as a co-catalyst (Entry 1, 95% yield), it was found that Me3SiCl alone is sufficient to achieve high efficiency (93%). The choice of the halogen in the aryl halide precursor significantly impacts the outcome: phenyl bromide is optimal (93%), whereas phenyl iodide results in a lower yield (77%, Entry 7) and phenyl chloride is completely unreactive (Entry 6). Furthermore, the silicon counterion is critical, as replacing Me3SiCl with Me3SiOTf leads to a dramatic decrease in yield to 33% (Entry 5).

reaction_process_description: For the synthesis of phenylalanine derivatives, benzylzinc bromide was prepared via a Reformatsky-type direct insertion. Benzyl bromide (0.75 mmol) was added to a suspension of zinc dust (1.0 mmol) in freshly distilled THF (3 mL) and stirred at room temperature for 0.5 hours. Subsequently, N,O-acetal 1a (0.50 mmol) and Me3SiCl (0.60 mmol) were added to the mixture. After stirring at room temperature, the reaction was quenched with saturated aqueous NaHCO3, extracted with CHCl3, and purified by flash chromatography to yield the phenylalanine derivative 3a in 96% isolated yield.
reaction_mechanism_logic: This reaction utilizes a Reformatsky-type approach where zinc metal inserts directly into the carbon-bromine bond of the benzyl halide to form the organozinc reagent. This avoids the use of strong bases like n-butyllithium. The resulting benzylzinc species then undergoes a coupling reaction with the N,O-acetal promoted by Me3SiCl activation, similar to the arylzinc series.
influence_analysis: The direct insertion method is highly effective for benzyl halides. The reaction demonstrates good functional group tolerance; substrates with electron-withdrawing groups such as methyl esters (3c, 79% yield) or aryl bromides (3d, 76% yield) are successfully converted to the corresponding phenylalanine derivatives, highlighting the chemoselectivity of the organozinc species compared to more reactive organometallics.

reaction_process_description: Phenylzinc bromide, generated via transmetalation from phenyl bromide and ZnBr2 in Et2O, was reacted with N,O-acetal 1c (0.50 mmol), which contains an N-phenylpiperazine moiety, in the presence of Me3SiCl (0.60 mmol). The reaction was stirred at room temperature, quenched with Na2CO3, and purified by silica gel chromatography to provide the coupling product 2i in 32% isolated yield.
reaction_mechanism_logic: The reaction scope was tested with different amine components in the N,O-acetal. In the case of the N-phenylpiperazine derivative 1c, the yield was significantly lower than with piperidine or diallylamine derivatives.
influence_analysis: The structure of the N,O-acetal substrate has a profound effect on reactivity. The authors attribute the low yield (32%) of 2i to the competitive coordination of Me3SiCl. Specifically, Me3SiCl appears to preferentially coordinate to the basic nitrogen of the N-phenylpiperazine ring rather than acting as an activator for the methoxy substituent, thereby inhibiting the intended coupling pathway.

reaction_process_description: To prepare an N-underivatized amino acid, the diallylamino-protected phenylalanine derivative 3e (0.50 mmol) was treated with 1,3-dimethylbarbituric acid (1.0 mmol) and a catalytic amount of Pd(PPh3)4 (0.025 mmol) in methanol (5 mL) at room temperature. The mixture was stirred for 3 hours, then quenched with 1 N HCl. After washing with CHCl3 and subsequent treatment with saturated aqueous Na2CO3, the organic layer was dried and evaporated to yield the N-unsubstituted phenylalanine derivative 6 in 70% yield.
reaction_mechanism_logic: This process involves a palladium-catalyzed deprotection of the diallylamino group. 1,3-dimethylbarbituric acid serves as a scavenger for the allyl groups released during the catalytic cycle. This sequence demonstrates that the Me3SiCl-promoted coupling can be integrated into a broader synthetic strategy to access primary amino acids.
influence_analysis: The use of the diallylamino group as a protecting moiety on the N,O-acetal allows for the successful synthesis of primary amino acid derivatives. The deprotection conditions (Pd-catalysis) are mild enough to preserve the methyl ester functionality, providing a practical route to N-unsubstituted amino acid esters.

reaction_process_description: Methyl bromoacetate (0.75 mmol) was reacted with zinc dust (1.0 mmol) in THF for 0.5 hours to generate the corresponding Reformatsky reagent. N,O-acetal 1a (0.50 mmol) and Me3SiCl (0.60 mmol) were then added. The reaction was stirred at room temperature, quenched with Na2CO3, and purified by flash chromatography to yield the aspartic acid derivative 5a in 99% isolated yield.
reaction_mechanism_logic: The reaction extends the methodology to α-halo esters, which form Reformatsky reagents upon treatment with zinc. These reagents are functionalized organozinc species that react efficiently with Me3SiCl-activated N,O-acetals to form aspartic acid derivatives.
influence_analysis: The Reformatsky reagent derived from methyl bromoacetate shows exceptional reactivity in this system, providing a nearly quantitative yield (99%). This demonstrates the high compatibility of the Me3SiCl-promoted coupling with ester-functionalized organozinc reagents, allowing for the facile synthesis of acidic amino acid skeletons.

reaction_process_description: In this reaction, methyl 2-(chloromethyl)-3-methylbut-2-enoate (1a) is reacted with a nucleophilic reagent prepared in situ from methyl lithium (MeLi), CuBr·Me2S, and ZnCl2. The organometallic reagent is formed in THF at -70 °C, warmed to 0 °C, and then reacted with substrate 1a. The mixture is stirred at -70 °C for 1 hour and then at 0 °C overnight. After quenching with brine and extraction with hexane, the crude product is purified by silica gel chromatography using a hexane/Et2O gradient to afford methyl 2-(tert-butyl)acrylate (2a) as a colorless oil in 86% isolated yield (94% GLC yield). The structure was confirmed by 1H-NMR and HR-MS.
reaction_mechanism_logic: The reaction follows an SN2' allylation mechanism. The authors observed that the combination of an organocuprate with ZnCl2 is essential for achieving complete allylic rearrangement, which allows for the generation of a quaternary carbon center at the C(2) position of the acrylate. This specific reagent system prevents the common side reaction of Michael addition to the product, as demonstrated by the quantitative recovery of 2a when subjected to the reaction conditions.
influence_analysis: The addition of ZnCl2 is the decisive factor for regioselectivity. In its absence, the reaction yields the SN2 substitution product rather than the desired SN2' allylic rearrangement product. The use of a slight excess of the nucleophile ensures high conversion without promoting Michael addition to the acrylate product.

reaction_process_description: This experiment compares the reactivity of organocopper reagents without zinc versus diorganozinc reagents. In Entry 3, reacting 1a with BuLi and CuBr·Me2S (without ZnCl2) results in the SN2 substitution product. In Entry 4, 1a is reacted with Bu2Zn (prepared from BuLi and ZnCl2) in THF with HMPA as a cosolvent. The reaction is stirred at -70 °C for 1 hour and then at room temperature for 24 hours, yielding methyl 2-(1,1-dimethylpentyl)prop-2-enoate (2b) in 91% yield.
reaction_mechanism_logic: The authors identified ZnCl2 as the critical component for allylic inversion. While the R2CuLi/ZnCl2 system is faster, the diorganozinc reagent (R2Zn) also provides high SN2' selectivity. However, the diorganozinc reaction is slower and requires the addition of HMPA to achieve high efficiency.
influence_analysis: The presence of HMPA as a cosolvent significantly enhances the reactivity of the diorganozinc species, allowing the reaction to proceed to high yield (91%) even though it is slower than the copper-mediated version.

reaction_process_description: Methyl propiolate (3) is converted to methyl 3-hydroxy-3-methyl-2-methylidenebutanoate (4a). DIBAH is added dropwise to HMPA in THF at 0 °C, followed by the addition of methyl propiolate. The resulting vinylaluminum intermediate is treated with acetone and BF3·Et2O. The mixture is stirred at 0 °C for 1 hour and then at room temperature for 20 hours. After workup with 1N HCl and NaHCO3, the product is purified by chromatography to give 4a in 74% yield.
reaction_mechanism_logic: The process involves the hydroalumination of the alkyne to form a [2-(methoxycarbonyl)vinyl]aluminum reagent. The subsequent Lewis-acid-promoted (BF3·Et2O) addition to acetone allows for the formation of the allylic alcohol. HMPA is used to modulate the reactivity of the aluminum species.
influence_analysis: The use of BF3·Et2O as a Lewis acid promoter is essential for the coupling of the vinylaluminum reagent with the ketone, ensuring the formation of the quaternary-substituted allylic alcohol.

reaction_process_description: Allylic alcohol 4a is converted to the allylic chloride 1a. N-chlorosuccinimide (NCS) and Me2S are reacted in CH2Cl2 at 0 °C to form a white suspension (chlorodimethylsulfonium chloride). A solution of 4a is added, and the mixture is stirred for 20 hours at 0 °C. After dilution with hexane and washing with brine, chromatography affords 1a in 94% yield.
reaction_mechanism_logic: This transformation utilizes the NCS/Me2S reagent system to effect an allylic rearrangement (SN2' substitution of the hydroxyl group by chloride). This method is highly selective for the rearranged allylic chloride over the direct substitution product.
influence_analysis: The NCS/Me2S system provides a mild and highly regioselective route to allylic chlorides with allylic transposition, which is a prerequisite for the subsequent SN2' alkylation step.

reaction_process_description: The synthesis of 2-organochalcogen-3-alkynylthiophenes (1) begins with the lithiation of 3-alkynylthiophene using 1.0 equivalent of n-butyllithium (1.5 M in hexane) in dry THF at -78 °C for 30 minutes. The mixture is warmed to -40 °C, and elemental chalcogen (Se or Te, 1.0 equiv.) is added. After stirring for 1 hour, an appropriate alkyl bromide (1.25 equiv.) is added at -10 °C, and the reaction is stirred for 2 hours at room temperature. The reaction is quenched with saturated NH4Cl, extracted with ethyl acetate, dried over MgSO4, and purified by flash chromatography on silica gel using hexane as the eluent.
reaction_mechanism_logic: The process involves a regioselective deprotonation at the C2 position of the thiophene ring, followed by nucleophilic attack of the resulting 2-lithiothiophene on elemental chalcogen to form a lithium chalcogenolate. Subsequent S_N2 alkylation with an alkyl bromide yields the 2-organochalcogen-3-alkynylthiophene precursor.
influence_analysis: The use of n-butyllithium at low temperatures ensures regioselective lithiation at the alpha-position of the thiophene. The sequential addition of chalcogen and alkyl halide allows for the modular installation of various organochalcogen groups.

reaction_process_description: In the optimization of the electrophilic cyclization, 2-butylseleno-3-(phenylethynyl)thiophene (1a, 0.25 mmol) was treated with iodine (I2, 1.1 equiv.) in 5 mL of CH2Cl2 at room temperature. The reaction reached completion in 5 minutes, providing the cyclized product 2a in 81% yield as determined by GC analysis.
reaction_mechanism_logic: The authors screened various solvents (CH2Cl2, THF, Et2O, MeOH, hexane, MeCN) to find the most efficient medium. CH2Cl2 was identified as the optimal solvent due to the significantly shorter reaction time (5 min) compared to THF (120 min) or Et2O (90 min), while maintaining high yields. The mechanism involves the electrophilic activation of the alkyne by I2, followed by nucleophilic attack from the selenium atom and subsequent dealkylation of the butyl group.
influence_analysis: The choice of solvent significantly impacts the reaction rate; CH2Cl2 provides the fastest kinetics. Furthermore, the nature of the group attached to selenium is critical: alkyl groups (butyl, ethyl) facilitate the cyclization, whereas a phenyl group (Entry 9) results in no reaction, likely due to the higher bond dissociation energy of the Se-Csp2 bond compared to the Se-Csp3 bond required for dealkylation.

reaction_process_description: Under optimized conditions, 2-butylseleno-3-(phenylethynyl)thiophene (1a) was reacted with I2 (1.1 equiv.) in CH2Cl2 at room temperature for 5 minutes. After the reaction, the mixture was washed with saturated aqueous Na2S2O3, extracted with CH2Cl2, dried over MgSO4, and purified by flash chromatography to afford 4-iodo-5-phenylselenopheno[2,3-b]thiophene (2a) in 76% isolated yield.
reaction_mechanism_logic: The scope study demonstrated that the reaction is general for various aryl and alkyl alkynes. The electronic nature of the substituents on the aryl ring (neutral, electron-donating, or electron-withdrawing) had little influence on the yield, suggesting that the rate-determining step or the transition state is not highly sensitive to the electronic density of the alkyne's aromatic partner.
influence_analysis: The high yield across various substrates indicates excellent functional group tolerance. However, benzothiophene derivatives required longer reaction times (up to 120 min) compared to simple thiophenes, and certain bulky or electronically deactivated benzothiophenes (Entries 20-22) failed to react.

reaction_process_description: To a Schlenk tube under argon containing p-tolylzinc chloride (1.5 mmol) was added 4-iodo-5-phenylselenopheno[2,3-b]thiophene (2a, 0.5 mmol) and Pd(PPh3)4 (0.057 g, 10 mol%). The mixture was stirred at room temperature for 3 hours. The solution was then diluted with CH2Cl2, washed with saturated NH4Cl, dried over MgSO4, and purified by flash chromatography (hexane) to yield 5-phenyl-4-p-tolylselenopheno[2,3-b]thiophene (5a) in 69% isolated yield.
reaction_mechanism_logic: This reaction utilizes a palladium-catalyzed Negishi cross-coupling to functionalize the C-I bond of the fused heterocycle. The organozinc reagent undergoes transmetallation with the palladium catalyst, followed by reductive elimination to form the new C-C bond.
influence_analysis: The use of 10 mol% Pd(PPh3)4 at room temperature is sufficient to achieve efficient coupling with the organozinc reagent, demonstrating the utility of the iodo-substituted fused heterocycle as a versatile synthetic intermediate.

reaction_process_description: A solution of 4-iodo-5-phenylselenopheno[2,3-b]thiophene (2a, 0.5 mmol) in a DMF/H2O mixture (5:1, 5 mL) was treated with 4-bromophenylboronic acid (1.5 equiv.), Pd(PPh3)4 (2 mol%), and K2CO3 (2 equiv.). The reaction mixture was stirred at reflux for 8 hours. After workup and purification by flash chromatography (hexane/ethyl acetate, 9:1), 4-(4-bromophenyl)-5-phenylselenopheno[2,3-b]thiophene (4a) was obtained in 63% isolated yield.
reaction_mechanism_logic: The Suzuki-Miyaura coupling allows for the introduction of an aryl group at the 4-position. The use of a base (K2CO3) and a polar solvent mixture (DMF/H2O) at reflux facilitates the transmetallation of the boronic acid.
influence_analysis: The reaction requires higher temperatures (reflux) and longer times (8 h) compared to the Negishi coupling, but it successfully tolerates an additional aryl bromide on the boronic acid partner, allowing for further potential functionalization.

reaction_process_description: 4-Iodo-5-phenylselenopheno[2,3-b]thiophene (2a, 0.5 mmol) was reacted with 4-chlorobenzenethiol (0.6 mmol) in dry dioxane (3 mL) in the presence of Et3N (1 mmol) and CuI (10 mol%). The mixture was stirred at reflux for 6 hours. Following workup and flash chromatography, 4-(4-chlorophenylthio)-5-phenylselenopheno[2,3-b]thiophene (3a) was isolated in 66% yield.
reaction_mechanism_logic: A copper-catalyzed C-S cross-coupling (Ullmann-type) is employed here. CuI serves as the catalyst to facilitate the nucleophilic substitution of the iodide by the thiolate generated in situ by Et3N.
influence_analysis: The copper-catalyzed conditions provide an efficient route to thio-substituted fused heterocycles, expanding the molecular complexity beyond C-C bond formations.

reaction_process_description: In this Heck-Matsuda arylation, enecarbamate 1 (5 mmol) was reacted with benzenediazonium tetrafluoroborate (1.3 equiv.) in acetonitrile (23 mL). The reaction was catalyzed by Pd2(dba)3 (4 mol-%) in the presence of sodium acetate (3 equiv.) at room temperature. The process was monitored by the evolution of N2 gas. After the reaction was complete, the mixture was filtered through silica gel and purified by flash chromatography using a hexanes/ethyl acetate gradient to yield the arylated product as an inseparable mixture of trans and cis diastereoisomers.
reaction_mechanism_logic: The reaction utilizes arenediazonium salts which undergo extremely facile oxidative addition with Pd(0) to generate a highly reactive cationic Ar-Pd(II) species under ligand-free conditions. The authors observed that the process is generally unselective (trans/cis ratio of 45:55), which they attribute to the stability of the cationic aryl palladium intermediate. Less stable intermediates are hypothesized to complex with the C-2 ester group, promoting migratory insertion from the same face.
influence_analysis: The use of a simple benzenediazonium salt results in a high isolated yield (85%), but the lack of a directing group or specific ligand leads to poor diastereoselectivity (45:55 trans/cis), which the authors intentionally exploited to create a stereochemically diverse library of ligands.

reaction_process_description: This reaction involves the catalytic asymmetric phenylation of p-tolualdehyde. First, the reactive organozinc species was generated in situ by reacting phenylboronic acid (0.72 mmol) with diethylzinc (2.1 mmol) in toluene at 60 °C for 12 h. After cooling to room temperature, the chiral ligand 5a (10 mol-%) was added. After 15 minutes of stirring, the mixture was cooled to 0 °C and p-tolualdehyde (0.3 mmol) was added. The reaction proceeded for 6 h before being quenched with water and saturated NH4Cl, followed by extraction with dichloromethane and purification by flash chromatography.
reaction_mechanism_logic: The optimization logic focused on temperature and ligand loading. The authors found that while the reaction at 25 °C gave high yield, the enantioselectivity was moderate (88:12 er). Lowering the temperature to 0 °C significantly improved the enantiomeric ratio to 98:2 without compromising the yield (98%). This suggests that the transition state for the enantioselective aryl transfer is highly temperature-dependent. Ligand 5a (trans-isomer) was identified as superior to its cis-counterpart 5b and the known ligand 11 at lower loadings (10 mol-%).
influence_analysis: Decreasing the reaction temperature from 25 °C to 0 °C resulted in a dramatic increase in enantioselectivity (from 88:12 to 98:2 er), which the authors attribute to a more organized transition state at lower temperatures. The 10 mol-% loading of ligand 5a is sufficient for high efficiency, outperforming traditional proline-based ligands that require 20 mol-% for similar results.

reaction_process_description: In this optimization experiment, the phenylation of p-tolualdehyde was conducted using ligand 5a (10 mol-%) at 0 °C in toluene, with the addition of 10 mol-% DiMPEG MW 2000 (dimethoxypolyethylene glycol) as an additive.
reaction_mechanism_logic: The authors tested DiMPEG, a common additive used to break up organozinc aggregates and improve enantioselectivity in related reactions. However, in this specific catalytic system involving triphenylprolinol ligands, the additive proved detrimental.
influence_analysis: The addition of DiMPEG resulted in a significant decrease in both yield (from 98% to 51%) and enantioselectivity (from 98:2 to 92:8 er). This indicates that the additive likely interferes with the formation of the active zinc-ligand complex or inhibits the boron-to-zinc exchange process.

reaction_process_description: The asymmetric phenylation of 2-furaldehyde was performed using the optimized conditions. Phenylboronic acid was converted to the organozinc reagent via boron-to-zinc exchange with Et2Zn in toluene. 2-Furaldehyde was then added to the mixture containing 10 mol-% of ligand 5a at 0 °C. The reaction was stirred for 6 h and purified to give the chiral heteroarylmethanol.
reaction_mechanism_logic: This reaction tests the functional group tolerance and substrate scope of the catalytic system, specifically focusing on heteroaromatic aldehydes. The high yield and er demonstrate that the catalyst is compatible with the coordinating furan ring.
influence_analysis: The use of a heteroaromatic substrate (2-furaldehyde) resulted in an excellent yield (89%) and high enantioselectivity (96:4 er), showing that the electronic properties of the furan ring do not negatively impact the chiral induction provided by ligand 5a.

reaction_process_description: This reaction involves the addition of a bulky aryl group to a heteroaromatic aldehyde. 4-Biphenylboronic acid was reacted with Et2Zn to generate the biphenylzinc reagent. This was then reacted with 2-furaldehyde in the presence of 10 mol-% ligand 5a at 0 °C in toluene.
reaction_mechanism_logic: The authors aimed to demonstrate the simultaneous variation of both the boronic acid (nucleophile) and the aldehyde (electrophile). The use of a bulky biphenyl group and a heteroaromatic aldehyde tests the limits of the catalyst's steric and electronic tolerance.
influence_analysis: The combination of a bulky biphenylboronic acid and 2-furaldehyde yielded the highest enantioselectivity observed in the study (98.5:1.5 er) with near-quantitative yield (98%). This suggests a strong structure-activity relationship where increased steric bulk on the aryl group can enhance the facial bias in the transition state.

reaction_id: Figure 3: NHC Ligand Optimization for sp3-sp3 Negishi Coupling
reaction_process_description: In this optimization study, 1-bromo-3-phenylpropane was reacted with n-butylzinc bromide (nBuZnBr) in a THF/NMP (2:1) solvent mixture at room temperature. The reaction utilized 2 mol% Pd2(dba)3 as the palladium source and 4 mol% of various imidazolium or 4,5-dihydroimidazolium salts (3–12) to generate the active NHC-Pd catalyst in situ. The reaction aimed to determine the effect of NHC ligand sterics on the yield of the cross-coupled product, n-heptylbenzene.
reaction_mechanism_logic: The study reveals a strong correlation between the steric bulk of the NHC ligand and catalytic activity. Subtle decreases in the sterics of the N-aryl substituents (e.g., moving from IPr to IMes) led to a dramatic decline in yield. The authors suggest that a monoligated NHC-Pd(0) species is the active catalyst, and an excess of ligand (2:1 L:Pd ratio) is required to ensure quantitative formation of this species in situ, protecting it from deactivation.
influence_analysis: The steric demand of the NHC ligand is the primary driver of reactivity; the bulky IPr ligand (3) provided an 85% yield, whereas the less sterically demanding IMes (9) resulted in only 3% yield. This indicates that large ortho-substituents on the aryl rings of the NHC are essential for stabilizing the active catalyst and promoting the coupling of unactivated sp3 centers.

reaction_process_description: Ethyl 4-bromobutyrate was coupled with n-butylzinc bromide in a THF/NMP (2:1) mixture at room temperature. The catalyst was generated in situ using 2 mol% Pd2(dba)3 and 4 mol% IPr·HCl. The reaction was allowed to proceed for 24 hours before workup and purification by flash chromatography to isolate the cross-coupled product, ethyl octanoate.
reaction_mechanism_logic: This reaction demonstrates the functional group tolerance of the in situ generated IPr-Pd catalyst system. The presence of an ester group on the alkyl bromide did not interfere with the coupling, highlighting the chemoselectivity of organozinc reagents compared to more reactive organolithium or Grignard reagents.
influence_analysis: The use of the bulky IPr ligand in a polar cosolvent system (THF/NMP) enables high efficiency (95% yield) for sp3-sp3 coupling while maintaining excellent tolerance for sensitive functional groups like esters.

reaction_id: Figure 5: LiBr Additive Study in sp3-sp3 Negishi Reaction
reaction_process_description: The coupling of 1-bromo-3-phenylpropane with nBuZnBr (prepared via Huo's iodine-catalyzed method) was investigated with varying amounts of LiBr additive. The reaction used 1 mol% Pd-PEPPSI-IPr as the precatalyst in THF/NMP at room temperature. The conversion was monitored as a function of LiBr equivalents relative to the organozinc reagent.
reaction_mechanism_logic: The reaction remains inactive until approximately 1.0 equivalent of LiBr is added, after which conversion increases exponentially. This suggests that the active transmetallating species is not the neutral RZnX but a higher-order zincate of the type [LimZn(R)Br3]^(2-m)-. Sequestration experiments with ZnBr2 (a LiBr 'sponge') confirmed that 'effective' LiBr concentration is the critical factor for initiating the catalytic cycle.
influence_analysis: The presence of LiBr is mandatory for the transmetallation step in sp3-sp3 Negishi couplings when using Pd-PEPPSI catalysts. Below 1.0 equivalent of LiBr, the reaction is completely inhibited, demonstrating that the formation of soluble, reactive zincate species is the 'on/off' switch for the reaction.

reaction_id: Table 5, Product 61: Pd-PEPPSI-IPent vs. IPr Comparison
reaction_process_description: The sterically hindered coupling between 2-bromo-m-xylene and mesitylzinc bromide (MesZnBr) was performed to compare the efficiency of first-generation Pd-PEPPSI-IPr and second-generation Pd-PEPPSI-IPent. The reaction was conducted in THF/NMP (2:1) at room temperature using 1 mol% catalyst loading.
reaction_mechanism_logic: Pd-PEPPSI-IPent (2) features a more sterically demanding NHC ligand (IPent) than IPr (1). This increased bulk facilitates the reductive elimination of sterically encumbered biaryls and stabilizes the monoligated active species. The IPent catalyst significantly outpaces the IPr analogue in forming tetra-ortho-substituted products.
influence_analysis: The transition from the IPr ligand to the more hindered IPent ligand results in a dramatic increase in reactivity for sterically crowded substrates, moving from 15% to 99% yield in the same timeframe. This highlights the 'structure-activity relationship' where increasing NHC bulk improves performance for hindered cross-couplings.

reaction_process_description: 2-Chloropyrazine was reacted with 2-pyridylzinc bromide in THF at room temperature for 24 hours. The reaction was catalyzed by 1 mol% Pd-PEPPSI-IPent. Unlike alkylzinc couplings, NMP was omitted and 1 equivalent of ZnCl2 was added to optimize the heteroaryl-heteroaryl coupling.
reaction_mechanism_logic: Heterocyclic substrates often require different conditions than simple aryl or alkyl partners. For Pd-PEPPSI-IPent, the omission of NMP and the addition of ZnCl2 were found to be beneficial for the coupling of electron-deficient heteroaryls, likely by modulating the transmetallation equilibrium and preventing catalyst inhibition by the heterocyclic nitrogens.
influence_analysis: The Pd-PEPPSI-IPent catalyst demonstrates high efficiency (91% yield) for challenging heteroaryl-heteroaryl couplings. The specific exclusion of NMP and the addition of ZnCl2 are critical optimization variables that enable the coupling of basic, electron-deficient heterocycles at room temperature.

reaction_process_description: In a one-pot procedure, n-butylzinc bromide was first prepared in situ from n-butyl iodide using Zn dust and LiCl in THF. Subsequently, ethyl 4-iodobenzoate and 1 mol% Pd-PEPPSI-IPr were added directly to the mixture. The coupling proceeded at 25 °C for 1 hour.
reaction_mechanism_logic: This 'one-pot' approach leverages Knochel’s LiCl-mediated zinc insertion to generate functionalized organozinc reagents that are then immediately used in the cross-coupling step. Pd-PEPPSI-IPr is highly compatible with the salts (LiCl) and residual zinc present in the mixture, outperforming traditional catalysts like Pd(PPh3)4.
influence_analysis: The integration of in situ reagent preparation with the highly active Pd-PEPPSI-IPr catalyst allows for extremely rapid (1 h) and efficient (95% yield) synthesis of functionalized products, demonstrating the practical utility of the precatalyst in streamlined synthetic sequences.

reaction_process_description: In this reaction, diethyl (1-ethoxycarbonyl)ethylphosphonate (3 mmol) was treated with n-butyllithium (3 mmol) in absolute THF (15 ml) at -78°C under nitrogen to generate the phosphoryl-stabilized carbanion. After stirring for 0.5 h, trifluoroacetic anhydride (3 mmol) was added in one portion. The mixture was stirred for 0.5 h at -78°C, then allowed to warm to 20°C. An organozinc reagent (9 mmol), prepared in situ from methyl bromoacetate (9 mmol) and zinc powder (9 mmol), was added. The mixture was stirred for 4 h, then quenched with 0.5 N HCl (15 ml). The product was extracted with ethyl ether, dried over Na2SO4, and purified by column chromatography (petroleum ether/ethyl acetate 99:2) to yield Z-ethyl 4-methoxycarbonyl-3-trifluoromethyl-2-methylbut-2-enoate (4a) in 66% isolated yield.
reaction_mechanism_logic: The reaction proceeds via a three-step consecutive process: deprotonation of the phosphonate, trifluoroacetylation to form a fluorinated intermediate, and subsequent nucleophilic addition of the organozinc reagent followed by the elimination of the phosphate anion. The Z-selectivity (100:0) is attributed to the trifluoromethyl group being cis to the ester group, which is confirmed by 19F NMR shifts appearing downfield (around -17.2 ppm).
influence_analysis: The amount of organozinc reagent significantly impacts the yield; increasing the equivalents from 1 to 3 (relative to the phosphonate) improved the yield from 45% to 66%. The methyl group (R) on the phosphonate substrate leads to exclusive Z-selectivity.

reaction_process_description: Following the general procedure, diethyl (1-ethoxycarbonyl)ethylphosphonate reacted with an organozinc reagent prepared from ethyl bromoacetate and zinc powder. The reaction yielded Z-ethyl 4-ethoxycarbonyl-3-trifluoromethyl-2-methylbut-2-enoate (4b) in 62% isolated yield after 4 hours of stirring at 20°C and purification via column chromatography.
reaction_mechanism_logic: The mechanism follows the same consecutive acylation-addition-elimination pathway. The 100% Z-selectivity is maintained, as evidenced by the 19F NMR signal at -17.0 ppm, indicating the trifluoromethyl group is cis to the ester moiety.
influence_analysis: Changing the ester group on the organozinc reagent from methyl (4a) to ethyl (4b) resulted in a slight decrease in yield (66% to 62%), while maintaining perfect Z-stereoselectivity.

reaction_process_description: Diethyl (1-ethoxycarbonyl)ethylphosphonate was reacted with an organozinc reagent derived from tert-butyl bromoacetate and zinc powder. The reaction produced Z-ethyl 4-t-butoxycarbonyl-3-trifluoromethyl-2-methylbut-2-enoate (4d) in 62% isolated yield. The product was characterized by 1H NMR and HRMS.
reaction_mechanism_logic: The reaction demonstrates the compatibility of bulky ester groups on the organozinc reagent. The Z-configuration is confirmed by the 19F NMR shift of -17.5 ppm.
influence_analysis: The use of a sterically hindered tert-butyl ester group on the organozinc reagent did not negatively impact the yield compared to the ethyl ester (both 62%), suggesting good tolerance for steric bulk in the nucleophile.

reaction_process_description: In this variation, allylzinc bromide (prepared from allyl bromide and zinc powder) was used as the organozinc reagent to react with the intermediate formed from diethyl (1-ethoxycarbonyl)ethylphosphonate and trifluoroacetic anhydride. This yielded the trifluoromethylated dienyl carboxylate, Z-ethyl 3-trifluoromethyl-2-methylhexa-2,5-dienoate (4e), in 57% isolated yield.
reaction_mechanism_logic: The use of an allylic organozinc reagent allows for the synthesis of diene systems. The Z-selectivity remains absolute (100:0), with the 19F NMR shift at -18.1 ppm.
influence_analysis: The introduction of an allyl group via the organozinc reagent successfully produces a 2,5-diene system, though the yield (57%) is slightly lower than those obtained with alpha-haloester-derived reagents.

reaction_process_description: Diethyl (1-ethoxycarbonyl-1-fluoromethyl)phosphonate was used as the substrate. It was treated with n-BuLi and trifluoroacetic anhydride, followed by reaction with the organozinc reagent derived from ethyl bromoacetate. This produced ethyl 4-ethoxycarbonyl-3-trifluoromethyl-2-fluorobut-2-enoate (4f) in 74% isolated yield with a Z:E ratio of 5:95.
reaction_mechanism_logic: When a fluorine atom is present at the alpha-position of the phosphonate (R=F), the stereochemical outcome shifts significantly toward the E-isomer (where F is trans to CF3). This is confirmed by 19F NMR coupling constants (4JFFtrans = 10 Hz).
influence_analysis: Replacing the alpha-methyl group with a fluorine atom on the phosphonate substrate increases the overall yield (from 62% in 4b to 74% in 4f) but reverses the predominant stereoselectivity from Z to E.

reaction_process_description: Diethyl (1-ethoxycarbonyl-1-fluoromethyl)phosphonate was reacted with allylzinc bromide. The reaction yielded ethyl 3-trifluoromethyl-2-fluorohexa-2,5-dienoate (4h) in 66% isolated yield with a Z:E ratio of 14:86.
reaction_mechanism_logic: The reaction combines the use of a fluorinated phosphonate and an allylic organozinc reagent. The E-isomer remains predominant, as determined by the 19F NMR data (trifluoromethyl shift at -15.6 ppm for the major isomer).
influence_analysis: The combination of an alpha-fluorine substrate and an allyl nucleophile results in a moderately high yield (66%) and maintains the E-selectivity characteristic of the fluorinated substrate series.

reaction_process_description: In this reaction, allyl phenyl ether (1a) underwent a regioselective bromination. The substrate was first treated with pyridinium tribromide (1.1 equiv.) in 1,2-dichloroethane (DCE) at room temperature for 12-14 hours to form a vicinal dibromide intermediate. Subsequently, DBU (3.1 equiv.) was added at 0 °C, and the mixture was heated to 60 °C to promote trans HBr elimination (Method A). The reaction was quenched with saturated aqueous NH4Cl and extracted with CHCl3. The product, 2-bromoallyl phenyl ether (2a), was obtained in 95% isolated yield after silica gel column chromatography.
reaction_mechanism_logic: The mechanism involves the formation of a vicinal dibromide followed by a DBU-promoted regioselective elimination of HBr. The regioselectivity is controlled by the inductive electron-withdrawing effect of the neighboring O-functional group, which directs the elimination to form the 2-bromoalkene rather than the 1-bromoalkene. Method A utilizes an excess of DBU to act as both a base and an HBr scavenger.
influence_analysis: The use of Method A (excess DBU) provides high efficiency for the bromination-elimination sequence. The inductive effect of the phenoxy group ensures nearly perfect regioselectivity (>99:1) for the C-2 position.

reaction_process_description: This reaction describes a one-pot three-step sequence starting from allyl phenyl ether (1a) to produce an enyne (3a). Following bromination by Method B (using 1.1 equiv. K2CO3 and 1.1 equiv. DBU in DCE), the reaction vessel was charged with CuI (10 mol-%), PdCl2(PPh3)2 (5 mol-%), Et3N (2.0 equiv.), and 1-heptyne (1.5 equiv.) at 0 °C. The mixture was stirred at room temperature for 12 hours. After workup and purification, the enyne product 3a was isolated in 31% yield.
reaction_mechanism_logic: The logic relies on the compatibility of the bromination/elimination conditions with the subsequent palladium-catalyzed Sonogashira coupling. Method B is preferred here because it reduces the amount of DBU required, which minimizes potential interference with the transition metal catalyst. The authors noted that the bromination conditions do not damage the catalyst, allowing the sequence to proceed in a single vessel.
influence_analysis: The yield of the Sonogashira coupling is relatively low (31%) in this specific entry, which the authors attribute to the sensitivity of the third step to coupling conditions. Specifically, excess palladium or elevated temperatures can trigger undesired allylic ionization of the O-functional group.

reaction_process_description: A one-pot Negishi methylation was performed on 1-(allyloxy)-4-methoxybenzene (1a). After bromination via Method A in acetonitrile, the mixture was treated with THF, PEPPSI-IPr (5 mol-%), and dimethylzinc (1.0 M in hexane; 6.0 equiv.) at 0 °C. The reaction was then heated to 60 °C for 2 hours. The reaction was quenched with H2O and extracted with ethyl acetate. The methylated product 4a was obtained in 48% isolated yield.
reaction_mechanism_logic: The Negishi coupling utilizes the highly active PEPPSI-IPr precatalyst to facilitate the methylation of the in situ generated 2-bromoalkene. Acetonitrile is used for the bromination, but THF must be added before the Negishi step to ensure the miscibility of the acetonitrile with the dimethylzinc/hexane solution.
influence_analysis: The addition of THF is a critical optimization variable to allow proper mixing of reagents. The yield is moderate (48%), and the authors observed that substrates with electron-withdrawing acyl or aryl groups on the oxygen tend to decompose during the Pd-mediated step, whereas electron-donating groups like the 4-methoxyphenyl group are better tolerated.

reaction_process_description: A one-pot Suzuki-Miyaura coupling was conducted starting from allyl phenyl ether (1a). After bromination by Method B in acetonitrile, a mixture of DMF/H2O (4:1), Pd(PPh3)4 (10 mol-%), K2CO3 (7.0 equiv.), and phenylboronic acid (3.0 equiv.) was added. The reaction was stirred at 100 °C for 1 hour. Following standard workup and silica gel chromatography, the arene product 5a was isolated in 58% yield.
reaction_mechanism_logic: The Suzuki-Miyaura step requires a polar solvent system (DMF/H2O) and a high temperature (100 °C) to facilitate the coupling between the 2-bromoalkene intermediate and the boronic acid. Method B is used for the initial bromination to maintain a cleaner environment for the Pd(PPh3)4 catalyst.
influence_analysis: The choice of Method B for the bromination step is significant; the authors noted that yields for the Suzuki-Miyaura coupling were lower when Method A was used. The high temperature (100 °C) is necessary for the efficiency of this specific coupling.

reaction_process_description: This reaction demonstrates the use of organotrifluoroborates in the one-pot Suzuki-Miyaura sequence. Starting from 1-(allyloxy)-4-nitrobenzene (1f), bromination was performed via Method B. Then, MeOH, PEPPSI-IPr (3 mol-%), K2CO3 (5.0 equiv.), and potassium phenyltrifluoroborate (3.0 equiv.) were added. The mixture was stirred at 75 °C for 6 hours. The product 5f was isolated in 75% yield.
reaction_mechanism_logic: Organotrifluoroborates are used as more stable and often more reactive alternatives to boronic acids. The use of PEPPSI-IPr as a catalyst allows the reaction to proceed at a lower temperature (75 °C) compared to the standard boronic acid conditions (100 °C).
influence_analysis: The use of potassium trifluoroborate salts combined with the PEPPSI-IPr catalyst resulted in a significantly higher yield (75%) compared to typical boronic acid couplings for similar substrates, highlighting the superior reactivity of the trifluoroborate/PEPPSI system in this one-pot methodology.

reaction_process_description: In a typical optimized procedure, 2-chloroquinoxaline (0.30 mmol) was reacted with triphenylbismuth (0.12 mmol, 0.4 equiv.) in the presence of Pd(PPh3)4 (0.015 mmol, 5 mol-%) and Cs2CO3 (0.60 mmol, 2 equiv.). The reaction was conducted in a 4:1 mixture of dry DMF and HMPA (4.5 mL) at 130 °C in a sealed tube under an argon atmosphere overnight. After cooling, the mixture was quenched with saturated aqueous NaHCO3, extracted with ethyl acetate, and purified by flash column chromatography on silica gel to afford 2-phenylquinoxaline in 72% isolated yield.
reaction_mechanism_logic: The optimization logic focused on maximizing the transfer of all three aryl groups from the bismuth reagent to improve atom economy. Initial screening showed that standard palladium catalysis (Pd(PPh3)4) was effective. Solvent screening revealed that while NMP and toluene were inferior to DMF, a DMF/HMPA mixture significantly enhanced the yield, likely due to the coordinating ability of HMPA which may assist in the transmetallation step or stabilize catalytic intermediates. The study also confirmed that the base (Cs2CO3) is necessary for optimal efficiency, although the reaction proceeds to a lesser extent (42%) without it.
influence_analysis: The choice of solvent mixture (DMF/HMPA 4:1) increased the yield from 65% (pure DMF) to 72%. The addition of a base (Cs2CO3) is critical, as its absence drops the yield from 65% to 42%. Increasing the temperature beyond 130 °C or using microwave irradiation at 170 °C resulted in lower yields (50% and 36% respectively), suggesting thermal degradation or side reactions at higher temperatures.

reaction_process_description: The cross-coupling of triphenylbismuth (0.4–0.7 equiv.) with various 2-halo(or 2-triflyl)azines and -diazines (including pyrazines, pyrimidines, pyridines, and pyridazines) was performed using Pd(PPh3)4 (5–10 mol-%) and Cs2CO3 (2 equiv.) in DMF or DMF/HMPA at 130 °C. The reaction tolerated a wide range of functional groups on the electrophile, such as esters, aldehydes, nitro groups, nitriles, ketones, and alcohols, providing the corresponding 2-arylheterocycles in yields ranging from 45% to 98%.
reaction_mechanism_logic: The substrate scope highlights the chemoselectivity of organobismuthanes. Unlike organomagnesium or organozinc reagents, the low polarity of the C–Bi bond allows for the presence of highly reactive electrophilic groups (like aldehydes and ketones) and acidic protons (like alcohols) on the coupling partners. The reactivity trend observed (2-bromopyridines > 2-chloropyridines) is consistent with a rate-determining oxidative addition step of the palladium catalyst into the C–X bond.
influence_analysis: The nature of the leaving group on the azine significantly influences reactivity: 2-bromo derivatives (e.g., 9b, 95%) are more reactive than 2-chloro analogues (e.g., 9a, 65%). 2-Triflyl groups show comparable reactivity to chlorides. The presence of electron-withdrawing groups (e.g., CN, NO2) or electron-donating groups (e.g., NH2) on the azine ring has little negative impact on the efficiency, demonstrating the robustness of the method.

reaction_process_description: 2,4-Dichloro-5-methylpyrimidine was reacted with triphenylbismuth (0.7 equiv.) under standard conditions (Pd(PPh3)4, Cs2CO3, DMF, 130 °C). The reaction selectively targeted the 4-position of the pyrimidine ring to yield the monophenylated product (4-phenyl-2-chloro-5-methylpyrimidine) in 60% yield, with minimal formation of the diphenylated product.
reaction_mechanism_logic: The regioselectivity is governed by the electronic environment of the pyrimidine ring. The 4-position is more electrophilic and susceptible to oxidative addition compared to the 2-position. By controlling the stoichiometry of the bismuth reagent (0.7 equiv.), the authors were able to favor the mono-coupling product over the di-coupling product, which was otherwise obtained as a mixture when using 0.4 equiv.
influence_analysis: Increasing the amount of Ph3Bi from 0.4 equiv. to 0.7 equiv. improved the yield of the mono-coupled product at the 4-position to 60% without significantly increasing the formation of the undesired diphenylated byproduct.

reaction_process_description: Functionalized triarylbismuthanes (bearing groups such as Me, OMe, Cl, CN, CO2Me, and acetals) and triheteroarylbismuthanes (2-thienyl, 3-quinolinyl) were coupled with 2-chloroquinoxaline. The reactions were carried out using 0.4–0.7 equiv. of the bismuth reagent, 5–10 mol-% Pd(PPh3)4, and 2 equiv. Cs2CO3 in DMF at 130 °C.
reaction_mechanism_logic: The study demonstrates that the electronic nature of the aryl group on the bismuth reagent (electron-neutral, withdrawing, or donating) has a relatively small impact on the coupling efficiency, with most substrates providing good to excellent yields. However, steric hindrance plays a significant role; ortho-substituted aryl groups (e.g., 18b) resulted in a lower yield (35%), suggesting that the transmetallation step is sensitive to steric bulk near the C–Bi bond.
influence_analysis: The position of the substituent on the aryl group is a key factor: para- and meta-substituted reagents typically gave yields >70%, whereas the ortho-methyl substituted reagent (18b) gave only 35%. This indicates that steric bulk at the ortho position significantly inhibits the reaction.

reaction_process_description: Tris[3-(1,3-dioxolan-2-yl)phenyl]bismuthane (18g) was subjected to acetal hydrolysis using aqueous HCl in THF. The reaction successfully liberated the aldehyde groups to produce tris(3-formylphenyl)bismuthane (20) in 75% yield. The product was characterized as a shelf-stable, air-insensitive solid.
reaction_mechanism_logic: This reaction demonstrates the remarkable stability of the C–Bi bond toward acidic and protic conditions. While many organometallic reagents (like organolithiums or Grignards) would undergo protodealkylation or decomposition under these conditions, the organobismuthane remains intact, allowing for functional group manipulation directly on the metal-bearing reagent. This provides a unique route to highly functionalized reagents that cannot be prepared via standard organometallic methods.
influence_analysis: The stability of the C–Bi bond under acidic conditions (aq. HCl) is the enabling factor for this synthesis, allowing the preparation of a reagent (20) that possesses three reactive aldehyde groups while maintaining its integrity as a triarylbismuthane.

reaction_process_description: Tris(3-formylphenyl)bismuthane (20, 0.4 equiv.) was coupled with 2-chloroquinoxaline (7a) using 5 mol-% Pd(PPh3)4 and 2 equiv. Cs2CO3 in DMF at 130 °C. The reaction yielded the corresponding cross-coupling product, 3-(quinoxaline-2-yl)benzaldehyde, in 80% isolated yield.
reaction_mechanism_logic: This reaction serves as a proof-of-concept for the transfer of highly reactive functional groups. The aldehyde group, which is typically incompatible with strong nucleophilic organometallics, remains untouched during the palladium-catalyzed cross-coupling. This highlights the 'mild reactivity' of organobismuthanes as a strategic advantage for chemoselective synthesis.
influence_analysis: The use of the pre-formed, stable formyl-functionalized bismuth reagent (20) allows for an 80% yield of the coupled product, demonstrating that the aldehyde group does not interfere with the catalytic cycle or the transmetallation process.

reaction_process_description: In this reaction, functionalized aryl iodides or bromides (ArX) are converted into the corresponding arylzinc species (ArZnX) using commercially available zinc dust and a catalytic amount of cobalt bromide (CoBr2). The reaction is performed in acetonitrile (CH3CN) as the solvent. The formation of the organozinc reagent is typically confirmed by quenching with iodine to form the aryl iodide, which is then analyzed by GC using an internal standard. This method is compatible with various electron-donating and electron-withdrawing groups in the para, meta, and ortho positions.
reaction_mechanism_logic: The mechanism involves the in situ generation of a low-valent cobalt(I) species from the reduction of CoBr2 by zinc dust. This Co(I) species undergoes oxidative addition into the aryl-halide bond. Subsequent transmetallation with zinc leads to the arylzinc halide. Acetonitrile is the preferred solvent for aryl iodides and bromides as it supports the stability of the active cobalt species during the insertion process.
influence_analysis: The use of acetonitrile as a solvent is critical for the formation of arylzinc species from bromides and iodides; however, it is insufficient for aryl chlorides because the low-valent cobalt(I) undergoes rapid disproportionation in this medium.

reaction_process_description: This procedure describes the synthesis of arylzinc reagents from less reactive aryl chlorides. The reaction utilizes zinc dust and CoBr2 in a mixture of acetonitrile and pyridine. This modification allows for the activation of aryl chlorides bearing electron-withdrawing groups, although it requires a higher catalyst loading (up to 33 mol%) and longer reaction times compared to aryl bromides.
reaction_mechanism_logic: The optimization logic centers on the stabilization of the low-valent cobalt(I) intermediate. In pure acetonitrile, Co(I) is unstable when reacting with slow-reacting aryl chlorides. The addition of pyridine as a co-solvent or additive coordinates to the cobalt center, stabilizing the Co(I) species and preventing disproportionation, thereby facilitating oxidative addition into the C-Cl bond.
influence_analysis: The addition of pyridine is the decisive factor enabling the activation of aryl chlorides; without it, the cobalt catalyst loses activity through disproportionation before the sluggish oxidative addition can occur.

reaction_process_description: Aryl triflates are converted into arylzinc triflates using zinc dust and a pre-formed cobalt complex, CoBr2(Bpy), in acetonitrile. This represents the first reported synthesis of organozinc triflates from phenol derivatives. The reaction is specifically designed to handle the unique reactivity profile of the triflate leaving group.
reaction_mechanism_logic: The use of the bipyridine (Bpy) ligand is essential for this transformation. The bipyridine coordinates strongly to the cobalt, creating a more robust and electronically tuned catalyst capable of inserting into the aryl-triflate bond, which is otherwise unreactive toward simple CoBr2/Zn systems.
influence_analysis: The bipyridine ligand is the key optimization variable; its presence is mandatory for the activation of aryl triflates, demonstrating a clear structure-activity relationship where ligand chelation enhances the catalyst's ability to activate strong C-O bonds.

reaction_process_description: Diarylmethanes are synthesized via a cobalt-catalyzed cross-coupling between aryl halides and benzyl chlorides. The reaction can be performed in a 'Barbier-fashion' where all reagents (aryl halide, benzyl chloride, zinc dust, and CoBr2) are mixed together in acetonitrile, or in a two-step procedure where the arylzinc is pre-formed. This method is highly functional group tolerant.
reaction_mechanism_logic: The reaction follows a Negishi-type coupling mechanism. The cobalt catalyst serves a dual purpose: first, it facilitates the formation of the arylzinc species from the aryl halide and zinc; second, it catalyzes the cross-coupling of this in situ generated arylzinc with the benzyl chloride. The Barbier-fashion protocol is preferred for reactive substrates to minimize side reactions like homocoupling.
influence_analysis: The Barbier-fashion addition method improves efficiency by allowing the arylzinc species to react with the benzyl chloride as soon as it is formed, which limits the accumulation of the organometallic reagent and reduces byproduct formation.

reaction_process_description: Styrene derivatives are synthesized through the vinylation of functionalized aryl halides with vinyl acetates. This chemical procedure uses cobalt bromide (CoBr2) associated with 2,2'-bipyridine as the catalyst and manganese (Mn) dust as the stoichiometric reducing agent. The reaction is conducted in a DMF/pyridine solvent mixture at 50°C.
reaction_mechanism_logic: Manganese reduces Co(II) to a low-valent Co(I) or Co(0) species, which is stabilized by the bipyridine ligand and potentially the vinyl acetate itself. Oxidative addition into the Ar-X bond forms an Ar-Co species, which then undergoes a substitution reaction with the vinyl acetate. A six-centered transition state is proposed to explain the regioselectivity toward alpha-substituted styrenes.
influence_analysis: The combination of bipyridine and pyridine is crucial; bipyridine is essential for the coupling to occur at all, while pyridine provides a significant rate acceleration, likely by assisting in the solvation and stabilization of the cobalt intermediates.

reaction_process_description: This reaction involves the direct alkylation of aryl bromides or chlorides with unreactive alkyl bromides containing beta-hydrogens. The catalytic system consists of CoBr2, a phosphine ligand (iPr2PhP), and manganese dust as the reductant. The reaction proceeds under mild conditions and tolerates various functional groups like esters and ketones.
reaction_mechanism_logic: The primary challenge in C(sp2)-C(sp3) coupling is preventing beta-hydride elimination from the alkyl-cobalt intermediate. The optimization of the ligand to iPr2PhP (diisopropylphenylphosphine) provides the necessary electronic and steric environment to stabilize the alkyl-aryl cobalt complex, allowing reductive elimination to occur faster than elimination.
influence_analysis: The choice of the phosphine ligand (iPr2PhP) is the critical optimization variable; it successfully suppresses the unproductive beta-hydride elimination pathway, which is a common failure mode for transition metal-catalyzed alkylations.

reaction_process_description: Aryl halides or triflates undergo conjugate addition (Michael addition) to methyl vinyl ketone (MVK). The reaction uses CoBr2(Bpy) as the catalyst, manganese as the reductant, and is performed in DMF at 80°C. A key feature is the slow addition of MVK, CoBr2(Bpy), and 0.5 equivalents of water to the reaction mixture.
reaction_mechanism_logic: The mechanism involves the formation of an arylcobalt species that adds to the electron-deficient olefin. The addition of water is a strategic optimization; it prevents the formation of a stable arylzinc intermediate (which would be unproductive for Michael addition) and instead promotes the catalytic cycle toward the 1,4-adduct.
influence_analysis: The presence of water and the slow addition technique are vital for high yields; water acts as a chemical switch that prevents the 'dead-end' formation of arylzinc species, while slow addition manages the concentration of the reactive MVK to minimize polymerization or side reactions.

reaction_process_description: In this reaction, ethyl 1,6-dimethyl-2-oxo-1,2-dihydropyrimidine-5-carboxylate (15b) was reacted with diethylzinc (Et2Zn) to synthesize ethyl 1,6-dimethyl-4-ethyl-2-oxo-1,2,3,4-tetrahydropyrimidine-5-carboxylate (16a). The procedure involved adding BF3·Et2O (1.0 equiv.) to a solution of the substrate (1 mmol) in dry toluene (30 mL) at 0 °C under an inert atmosphere. After stirring for 30 min, neat diethylzinc (3 mmol) was added, and the mixture was allowed to warm to room temperature and stir for 48 h. The reaction was quenched with saturated aqueous NH4Cl, extracted with dichloromethane, and the crude product was purified by column chromatography using ethyl acetate/hexane as eluent. The product was obtained as a white solid in 70% isolated yield and characterized by IR, 1H NMR, 13C NMR, and HRMS.
reaction_mechanism_logic: The reaction relies on the Lewis acid activation of the imine moiety within the 1,2-dihydropyrimidine core. Molecular orbital calculations at the HF/6-31G* level demonstrated that coordination of BF3·OEt2 to the ureido carbonyl and nitrogen atoms significantly increases the natural atomic charge (electrophilicity) of the azomethine carbon (C-4). This activation overcomes the inherent low electrophilicity of the C=N bond compared to C=O. The regioselectivity is exclusively directed to the C-4 position, likely due to the stabilization of the resulting negative charge on the nitrogen atom by the adjacent ureido carbonyl group.
influence_analysis: The addition of BF3·OEt2 is critical; without this Lewis acid activator, the reaction provides poor yields. The choice of solvent is also paramount, as toluene was found to be superior to polar solvents like THF or DCM, which resulted in poor yields. The regioselectivity is perfect, with no addition observed at other positions, attributed to the electronic activation of the C-4 imine carbon.

reaction_process_description: This reaction describes the synthesis of ethyl 1,6-dimethyl-4-phenyl-2-oxo-1,2,3,4-tetrahydropyrimidine-5-carboxylate (16j) by the addition of diphenylzinc to ethyl 1,6-dimethyl-2-oxo-1,2-dihydropyrimidine-5-carboxylate (15b). Diphenylzinc was generated in situ by adding diethylzinc (3.0 mmol) dropwise to a solution of triphenylborane (1.0 mmol) in dry toluene at ambient temperature and stirring for 30 min. This mixture was then transferred to a solution of the substrate (1 mmol) in dry toluene at 0 °C. The reaction was stirred for 48 h, quenched with NH4Cl, extracted with DCM, and purified via column chromatography to yield the product in 70% isolated yield.
reaction_mechanism_logic: Unlike the alkylzinc additions that require BF3·OEt2, the arylation utilizes diphenylzinc generated in situ via transmetallation between BPh3 and Et2Zn. Triphenylborane likely serves a dual role as both the source of the phenyl group and a Lewis acid activator for the pyrimidine core. The high regioselectivity for the C-4 position is maintained, consistent with the electronic activation of the azomethine carbon.
influence_analysis: The in situ generation of diphenylzinc from BPh3 and Et2Zn is an effective method for introducing aryl groups. The reaction efficiency (70% yield) is comparable to the alkylation, demonstrating that the transmetallation approach provides sufficient reagent activity and activation of the substrate without the need for additional BF3·OEt2.

reaction_process_description: In this reaction, ethyl 1-methyl-6-phenyl-2-oxo-1,2-dihydropyrimidine-5-carboxylate (15d) was reacted with diethylzinc to produce ethyl 1-methyl-6-phenyl-4-ethyl-2-oxo-1,2,3,4-tetrahydropyrimidine-5-carboxylate (16m). Following the general procedure for alkylzinc reagents, the substrate (1 mmol) in toluene was activated with BF3·OEt2 (1 mmol) at 0 °C, followed by the addition of Et2Zn (3 mmol). After 48 h at room temperature and standard workup/purification, the product was isolated in 80% yield.
reaction_mechanism_logic: The mechanism follows the Lewis acid activation model. Interestingly, the presence of a phenyl group at the C-6 position of the substrate (R2 = Ph) appears to enhance the reaction efficiency compared to the C-6 methyl analogues. This suggests a structure-activity relationship where the electronic or steric environment provided by the 6-phenyl group facilitates the regioselective addition at C-4.
influence_analysis: The substitution at the C-6 position of the pyrimidine core significantly influences the yield. Substrates with a 6-phenyl group (15d) consistently provided higher yields (72-80%) for various organozinc reagents compared to those with a 6-methyl group (63-70%), indicating that the C-6 substituent modulates the reactivity of the activated imine system.

reaction_process_description: This entry summarizes the scope of the reaction for various combinations of substrates (15a-d) and organozinc reagents (diethyl, di-n-propyl, di-n-butyl, and diphenylzinc). For alkylzinc reagents (16b-i, 16n-o), BF3·OEt2 was used as the activator in toluene. For phenylzinc reagents (16k-l, 16p), the in situ BPh3/Et2Zn method was employed. All reactions were conducted on a 1 mmol scale in toluene for 48 h, yielding the corresponding C-4 substituted DHPMs in isolated yields ranging from 63% to 78%.
reaction_mechanism_logic: The consistent regioselectivity across a diverse range of alkyl and aryl zinc reagents confirms the robustness of the Lewis acid activation strategy. The authors observed that varying the ester group (methyl, ethyl, isopropyl) on the substrate had minimal impact on the yield, whereas the C-6 substituent (Me vs Ph) and the nature of the organozinc reagent were the primary factors affecting performance.
influence_analysis: The study reveals a clear trend: 6-phenyl substituted substrates are more reactive than 6-methyl ones. Furthermore, the necessity of toluene as a non-polar solvent and BF3·OEt2 as an activator for alkylzinc reagents defines the optimal conditions for this regioselective transformation. Steric bulk in the organozinc reagent (e.g., n-butyl vs ethyl) or the substrate ester group (e.g., isopropyl vs methyl) resulted in only marginal decreases in yield.

reaction_process_description: In this reaction, benzoyl chloride (1 equiv.) in CH2Cl2 was added dropwise to a solution of 2-amino-2-methyl-1-propanol (2 equivs.) in CH2Cl2 at 0°C. After stirring overnight at 25°C, the mixture was evaporated to yield N-(2-hydroxy-1,1-dimethylethyl)benzamide (2) as a white sticky solid. This intermediate was then treated with excess thionyl chloride (SOCl2) at 0°C for 3 hours to effect cyclization. The resulting hydrochloride salt was neutralized with aqueous NaOH, extracted with ether, and purified by vacuum distillation to give 2-phenyl-4,4-dimethyl-2-oxazoline (3) as a colorless oil in 62.8% yield.
