reaction_process_description: In a Negishi cross-coupling reaction, the organozinc reagent 2a (1.2 mmol in DME) was added to a solution of p-iodotoluene (1.5 mmol) in DME (4 mL) at -10 °C. The reaction was catalyzed by Pd2(dba)3 (2.5 mol%) and P(o-tol)3 (10 mol%), with CuBr·SMe2 (0.1 equiv) added as a co-catalyst/additive. The mixture was allowed to slowly warm to room temperature overnight. After workup with water and brine and purification by flash chromatography (hexanes/AcOEt 4:1), the phenylalanine derivative 3 was obtained as a colorless solid.
reaction_mechanism_logic: This reaction served as the initial optimization point for the coupling of serine-derived organozinc reagents. DME was utilized as the solvent for this standard aryl iodide substrate. The addition of CuBr·SMe2 is a known strategy in Negishi couplings to facilitate transmetallation from zinc to palladium via an intermediate organocopper species.
influence_analysis: The combination of a palladium catalyst with a triorthotolylphosphine ligand and a copper(I) additive in DME allowed for the successful coupling of the alkylzinc reagent with a simple aryl iodide, providing a moderate yield of 66%.

reaction_process_description: The organozinc reagent 2a (1.2 mmol) was coupled with the electron-rich substrate p-iodoaniline (1.5 mmol). The reaction was performed in a 1:1 mixture of HMPT and THF (4 mL) at -10 °C, warming to room temperature overnight. The catalyst system comprised Pd2(dba)3 (2.5 mol%), P(o-tol)3 (10 mol%), and CuBr·SMe2 (0.1 equiv). Following standard workup and purification by silica gel chromatography (hexanes/AcOEt 3:2), the product Z-p-NH2-Phe-OtBu 4 was isolated as a yellowish glass.
reaction_mechanism_logic: The authors found that while DME was suitable for p-iodotoluene, the more electron-rich p-iodoaniline required a more polar solvent system. Switching to a mixture of HMPT and THF (1:1) was necessary to achieve efficient coupling with this more challenging, electron-donating substrate.
influence_analysis: The use of a highly polar solvent mixture (HMPT/THF) was the key optimization variable that enabled the coupling of an electron-rich iodoaniline, resulting in an improved yield (73%) compared to the standard conditions used for p-iodotoluene.

reaction_process_description: Organozinc reagent 2b (1.1 mmol, derived from Z-I-Ala-OMe) was reacted with p-iodo-Boc-aniline (1.2 mmol) in a 1:1 HMPT/THF solvent mixture. The reaction employed Pd2(dba)3 (2.5 mol%), P(o-tol)3 (10 mol%), and CuBr·SMe2 (0.1 equiv). The mixture was warmed from -10 °C to room temperature overnight. Purification via silica gel chromatography (hexanes/AcOEt 2:1) yielded the protected amino acid 5 as a solid.
reaction_mechanism_logic: This reaction demonstrates the compatibility of the optimized HMPT/THF protocol with Boc-protected amino groups on the aryl iodide partner, further extending the scope to protected phenylalanine derivatives.
influence_analysis: The HMPT/THF solvent system effectively supports the coupling of N-Boc protected iodoanilines, maintaining high yields (75%) and demonstrating good functional group tolerance.

reaction_process_description: The synthesis of a metal-chelating amino acid was achieved by coupling organozinc reagent 2a (1.2 mmol) with aryl iodide 9 (1.2 mmol), which bears a protected iminodiacetate (IDA) moiety. The reaction was conducted in HMPT/THF (1:1) using Pd2(dba)3 (2.5 mol%), P(o-tol)3 (10 mol%), and CuBr·SMe2 (0.1 equiv). The reaction was initiated at -10 °C and allowed to reach room temperature overnight. Purification by chromatography (hexanes/AcOEt 7:3) afforded product 6.
reaction_mechanism_logic: The goal was to extend the Negishi coupling to aryl iodides containing complex chelating side chains. Aryl iodide 9 was prepared from p-iodobenzyl bromide and dimethyl iminodiacetate. The established HMPT/THF conditions were applied to facilitate the C-C bond formation in the presence of the tertiary amine and ester groups of the IDA ligand.
influence_analysis: The protocol successfully tolerates the iminodiacetate functional group, allowing for the direct synthesis of a phenylalanine derivative with a metal-chelating side chain in 65% yield.

reaction_process_description: Organozinc reagent 2b (0.35 mmol) was coupled with aryl iodide 8 (0.28 mmol), which features a tri-Boc protected cyclen ligand. The reaction was performed in HMPT/THF (1:1) with Pd2(dba)3 (2.5 mol%), P(o-tol)3 (10 mol%), and CuBr·SMe2 (0.1 equiv). The mixture was warmed from -10 °C to room temperature overnight. After workup and purification by silica gel chromatography (hexanes/AcOEt 3:2), the cyclen-modified amino acid 7 was obtained as a solid.
reaction_mechanism_logic: This reaction represents the most complex substrate in the study, involving a bulky cyclen-substituted benzyl iodide. The high yield suggests that the Negishi coupling conditions are robust even for sterically demanding and highly functionalized aryl iodides.
influence_analysis: Despite the significant steric bulk and the presence of multiple protected nitrogen atoms in the cyclen ring, the reaction provided the highest yield in the series (86%), demonstrating the excellent compatibility of the Negishi coupling with complex metal-chelating architectures.
